\[\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 7 & -3 \end{pmatrix}\]to $S,$ we obtain the region $S'.$  Find the area of $S'.$

answer:
To find the area of the region \( S' \) after applying the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 7 & -3 \end{pmatrix}\) to the original region \( S \) with area 10, we need to calculate the absolute value of the determinant of the matrix and multiply it by the original area.

The determinant of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 7 & -3 \end{pmatrix}\) is calculated as follows:
\[
\text{det} = (2 \cdot -3) - (1 \cdot 7) = -6 - 7 = -13
\]

The absolute value of the determinant is \( |-13| = 13 \).

Multiplying this absolute value by the original area of 10 gives:
\[
10 \times 13 = 130
\]

Thus, the area of the transformed region \( S' \) is \(\boxed{130}\).
